title: 🏛️ Exams 2011–2026 · one root, several words: noun, adjective or adverb ⭐⭐⭐

questions.prompt: (Exam 2011, general) A text about shopping on the Internet says it is a convenient way of finding information, "but you just need to be ___."
questions.explanation: After be, the gap describes the person, you, so it needs an adjective: careful, which is the noun care with the ending -ful. Care is the noun, and carefully, with -ly, would tell how an action is done.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2019, general) A text about volunteering says that it helps people while "developing important ___ skills."
questions.explanation: The gap stands before the noun skills, so it needs an adjective: social, the adjective of the word society. Society is a noun, and socially, with -ly, would tell how an action is done.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2018, general) A grown-up remembers the first day of school and speaks to the reader now: "I ___ everyone to cherish those days because if you don't, then you will regret it." Advice is the noun, a piece of guidance, and advise is the verb, to give advice.
questions.explanation: After the subject I, the gap needs a verb in the present: advise. Advice is a noun and advisor is a person, so neither can follow I. Advised is a past form, but the speaker is giving the advice now.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2025, general) A text about household chores says that children learn relationship skills "like communicating ___, negotiating, cooperating and working as a team."
questions.explanation: The gap tells how children communicate, so it is an adverb: the adjective clear + -ly. Clear describes a noun, and clearer is a comparative that would need than.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2024, technical) A text about Monique Strong says: "Her father was involved in the ___ industry in California."
questions.explanation: After the and before the noun industry, the gap names the kind of industry, so it is a noun: construction, from the verb construct with the ending -tion. Constructed and constructs are verb forms, and a verb cannot stand there.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2025, technical) A text about technical education says that it "creates more and more ___ opportunities", that is, more chances to find a job.
questions.explanation: The gap names the situation of having a job, so it is a noun in -ment, from the verb employ: employment opportunities. An employer and an employee are people, a boss and a worker, not a kind of opportunity.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2026, technical) A man describes the people in his local store: "the place is filled with younger ___, roofers and builders getting their drinks."
questions.explanation: The gap names a group of workers, like roofers and builders, so it is a person noun in -er, in the plural: plumbers. Plumbing is the trade, not the people who do it, plumb is the root, and the singular plumber cannot stand alone after younger.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2026, general) A text presents Prasiddhi, a 12-year-old girl who has planted thousands of trees across India: "This determined ___ has become one of the country's most famous nature lovers."
questions.explanation: The gap follows the adjective determined and is the subject of has become, so it names a person: a noun in -ist. Environmental is an adjective and environmentally is an adverb, and neither can be the subject of a verb.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2022, technical) Joan left her job as a waitress to follow a training program in construction. Complete the sentence: "Joan is proud of her ___ and has become an active member in her community."
questions.explanation: After her, the gap is a noun: the thing she decided. It is built on the verb choose, but it changes more than its ending. Choose is the verb, chosen is the participle, and choosing needs an object to say what she chose, so only the noun fits.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2022, general) Put the word in brackets in the right form: "Many (fame) ___ faces are helping out by launching daily lessons on their social media accounts."
questions.explanation: The gap stands before the noun faces, so it needs an adjective. The ending that makes an adjective of this kind of root is -ous, and the silent e of the root disappears before it.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2022, general) Put the word in brackets in the right form: "Music has always been seen as an (excite) ___ subject."
questions.explanation: The gap stands before the noun subject, so it needs an adjective, and the subject is the thing that causes the feeling, not the person who feels it. The ending for the cause is -ing, and the silent e of the root drops before it.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2025, general) Put the word in brackets in the right form: "They are hooked up to a tablet or laptop for (entertain) ___, or with their heads bent over a small device."
questions.explanation: The gap follows the preposition for and names a thing, so it needs a noun, not a verb form. The noun is built by adding the ending -ment to the verb; the -ing form would describe something that amuses people, not the amusement itself.
